minutes.headline: Finance Committee backed a letter supporting the open space report and set its budget-season meeting calendar.
minutes.summary: The committee discussed the town's open space and recreation plan, with questions on cost, grant eligibility and the Community Preservation Act, and voted to send a letter of support. It then reviewed the draft FY20 budget-season calendar, snow-date options, and how to handle a long warrant public hearing. Members also heard capital planning highlights, a ClearGov dashboard update, free cash and tax rate notes, and approved three sets of minutes.

votes.motion: Support the open space report process and have a member write and sign a letter of support on the committee's behalf

budget_items.what_was_said: The plan has no upfront cost and positions the town to apply for state grants. Any later projects would go through the budget process.
A member noted the CPA would raise taxes and would need a separate town vote. It was described as a way to fund priorities, not a priority itself.
Stewardship and forestry planning is paid from the Conservation Commission's timber revolving fund.
The town signed on with ClearGov for a budget dashboard and budget software; the insights portion was said to cost about an amount for this year.
Free cash was certified at roughly a stated range, and none has been used yet.
The final excess levy capacity left was stated.
The capital planning committee tentatively approved nine requests, with items including asbestos abatement, a DPW fuel tank removal and two police cruisers.
The engine and rescue vehicle were not approved yet; the chief spent on a pump repair instead of replacement.

decisions.decision: Budget season calendar to follow last year's pattern, with school and town departments not on the same night.
Alternate Monday dates to be posted as snow makeup nights for Thursday budget meetings, subject to room availability.
Warrant public hearing to be scheduled for two nights on the Monday and Thursday, since the warrant closes too late to decide in advance.
Departments to be asked to email presentation materials about 48 hours ahead of budget reviews.
Time to be set aside at the end of each budget review to discuss points for the Finance Committee report.
Budget dashboard presentation postponed, likely handled in a non-televised workshop, probably not before spring.
Next meeting set for January 10th, with no meeting Christmas week.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted to support the open space report process and to send a letter of support signed by a member on its behalf.
The committee agreed to follow last year's budget-season pattern, with school and town departments not scheduled on the same night.
Alternate Monday dates are to be posted as snow makeup nights for Thursday budget meetings, subject to room availability.
The warrant public hearing is to be scheduled for two nights, Monday and Thursday, because the warrant closes too late to decide in advance.
The capital planning committee tentatively approved nine requests; the fire engine and rescue vehicle were not yet approved. Next meeting is January 10th.

why_it_matters: The open space plan has no upfront cost but positions the town to apply for state grants, and any later project would come through the budget process; the Community Preservation Act would raise taxes and need its own town vote.
The calendar and hearing arrangements set when residents can attend and comment on department budgets and the warrant, including makeup nights if snow cancels a Thursday session.
Capital requests still pending, such as the fire engine and rescue vehicle, could affect borrowing and free cash use in the coming budget.
watch_next: Next Finance Committee meeting on January 10th; none is planned Christmas week.
Posting of the alternate Monday snow dates and the two-night warrant public hearing schedule.
